title: Trajectory through a phase host
statement: Let $I$ index phase state sets $\mathrm{Ph}(i)$ and machines $M_i$, let $q_0$ be a state in their disjoint union, and let $red$ assign to each phase and state either no successor or a state in that union. Fix a phase $p$, a state $s_0\in\mathrm{Ph}(p)$, a contract $C$ for $M_p$ with exit set $X$, a datum $i$, and a host configuration $d$ whose state is $(p,s_0)$. Assume that the halted state is not in $X$, every state outside $X$ reduces to no successor in phase $p$, every state in $X$ reduces to a state in a different phase, and the configuration obtained from $d$ by replacing its state with $s_0$ satisfies $C$'s precondition. Through and including $C$'s assigned time, the host run agrees with the run of $M_p$ from that state-replaced configuration, with states embedded in phase $p$. One step later, the host run equals the endpoint of $C$ with its state bound through $red$; moreover, that endpoint has a state belonging to $X$.
hypotheses_covered: A family of phase-indexed machines and phase state sets
$C$ is a contract for $M_p$ with exit set $X$
The halted state is not in $X$
States outside $X$ reduce to no successor in phase $p$
States in $X$ reduce to states in a different phase
The host configuration starts in state $(p,s_0)$
replaced:
Let $M_r$ be a machine for each phase $r$, let the host machine have initial state
$q_0$, and let the reduction map send a phase and state to an optional phase-state pair.
Fix a phase $p$, a state $s_0$ in that phase, a contract $C$ for $M_p$ with exit set
$X$, and a parameter $i$ and host configuration $d$ whose state is $(p,s_0)$. Assume the
halted state is not in $X$, every state outside $X$ reduces to no successor in phase
$p$, and every state in $X$ reduces to a successor in a different phase; also assume the
phase-$p$ projection of $d$ satisfies $C$'s precondition. Up to and including time $C$'s
specified duration, the host run equals the run of $M_p$ on that projection with its
state mapped into phase $p$; one step later it equals the endpoint of $C$ with its state
bound through the reduction map; and that endpoint has a state belonging to $X$.
